#### `filler` {#filler}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The block filling the hollow core of the geode.**

Usually air, which is what makes the geode hollow.

#### `inner_layer` {#inner_layer}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The block lining the inside of the shell.**

Each lining cell is either this or alternate_inner_layer, decided per cell by use_alternate_layer0_chance.

#### `alternate_inner_layer` {#alternate_inner_layer}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The second lining block, mixed into the inner layer.**

It is also the layer inner_placements can grow on when placements_require_layer0_alternate is set.

#### `middle_layer` {#middle_layer}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The block of the shell's middle band.**

Sits between the lining and the outer skin.

#### `outer_layer` {#outer_layer}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The block of the shell's outermost band.**

This is the surface the geode presents to the surrounding stone.

#### `inner_placements` {#inner_placements}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · blockList</p>

**Blocks scattered on the inside of the lining -- the crystals.**

One entry is picked at random per chosen position, and the position still has to be able to hold it.

#### `min_outer_wall_distance` {#min_outer_wall_distance}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer · range [1, 10]</p>

**The smallest offset a lump may take from the geode's centre.**

Each lump is offset by a draw from this UP TO BUT NOT INCLUDING max_outer_wall_distance, made separately for x, y and z -- so 4/6 gives 4 or 5, and 4/5 is always 4.

#### `max_outer_wall_distance` {#max_outer_wall_distance}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer · range [1, 20]</p>

**The largest offset a lump may take from the geode's centre.**

It does double duty: it also divides into the number of lumps to set the shell thresholds, so raising it changes the thickness of the shell as well as how far the lumps spread.

#### `min_distribution_points` {#min_distribution_points}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer · range [1, 10]</p>

**The fewest lumps the geode is built from.**

Drawn once per geode, from this UP TO BUT NOT INCLUDING max_distribution_points -- vanilla's 3/4 is always 3, and 4/6 gives 4 or 5, never 6.

#### `max_distribution_points` {#max_distribution_points}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer · range [1, 20]</p>

**The most lumps the geode is built from.**

More points make a lumpier, less spherical geode -- but this value is never itself drawn: the count stops one short of it, so 4 is the most a 3/5 pair ever produces.

#### `min_point_offset` {#min_point_offset}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer · range [0, 10]</p>

**The low end of a per-lump value that varies how strongly each lump shapes the geode.**

Drawn once per lump, from this UP TO BUT NOT INCLUDING max_point_offset. Unless max is strictly above min there is no draw at all and every lump takes 0 -- not this value.

#### `max_point_offset` {#max_point_offset}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer · range [0, 10]</p>

**The high end of a per-lump value that varies how strongly each lump shapes the geode.**

Drawn once per lump, from min_point_offset UP TO BUT NOT INCLUDING this. Unless it is strictly above min there is no draw at all and every lump takes 0, whatever min says.

#### `max_radius` {#max_radius}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer</p>

**How far from the origin the geode is allowed to reach.**

It is the size of the box that gets examined, not the size of the geode: every column within it is tested and most of them come out empty. Raising it costs work whether or not the geode gets any bigger.

#### `crack_point_offset` {#crack_point_offset}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer · range [0, 10]</p>

**Widens the opening cracked into the geode's shell.**

Added to the distance test that decides which cells the crack carves away.

#### `generate_crack_chance` {#generate_crack_chance}

<p class="fl-facts">required · number · range [0, 1]</p>

Schema-required and validated, but not read anywhere in the engine's placement routine that has been located -- the crack roll it looks like it controls is a hardcoded 0.95 compare.

#### `base_crack_size` {#base_crack_size}

<p class="fl-facts">required · number · range [0, 5]</p>

Schema-required and validated, but not read during placement -- see generate_crack_chance.

#### `noise_multiplier` {#noise_multiplier}

<p class="fl-facts">required · number</p>

**How strongly noise distorts the shell.**

At 0 the geode is a smooth set of merged spheres; raising it makes the boundary between the layers ragged.

#### `use_potential_placements_chance` {#use_potential_placements_chance}

<p class="fl-facts">required · number · range [0, 1]</p>

**Chance that a lining cell is put forward as somewhere to grow inner_placements.**

Rolled per lining cell, and only within the lining band.

#### `use_alternate_layer0_chance` {#use_alternate_layer0_chance}

<p class="fl-facts">required · number · range [0, 1]</p>

**Chance that a lining cell uses alternate_inner_layer instead of inner_layer.**

Rolled per lining cell, which is what mixes the two blocks through the lining.

#### `placements_require_layer0_alternate` {#placements_require_layer0_alternate}

<p class="fl-facts">required · boolean</p>

**Restricts inner_placements to cells that came out as the alternate lining block.**

With it off, both lining blocks can carry them.

#### `invalid_blocks_threshold` {#invalid_blocks_threshold}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer</p>

**How many unusable distribution points to tolerate before abandoning the geode.**

Reaching it stops the whole placement on the spot -- nothing is built. Staying below it is harmless: an unusable point is still kept and still shapes the geode.
